title: Velocity moodboard — weekly check and micro-retro
content:
Purpose / context:
This is my compact weekly check — think of it as a 15–20 min micro-retro + a tactical plan for next week. Keep it short. The goal is to surface trends in velocity, energy, and blockers so I can adjust scope and habits before things pile up.

Time window: Mon 2026-03-02 -> Sun 2026-03-08

Snapshot (quick bullets):
- Focused deep-work hours: target 12, actual ~7.5 (too many meetings + context switches)
- PRs merged: target 4, actual 2 (one big infra PR still in review)
- Customer/ops handoffs completed: 3 (good)
- Blocker time: ~6 hours spent debugging production KV cache edge-case
- Mood / energy: 6/10 mid-week slump, recovered Friday with a 2 hour deep block

Personal KPI table (my simple view):
- Deep hours: target=12, last week=7.5, trend=down ↘
- PR throughput: target=4, last week=2, trend=flat ↔
- Meeting minutes: target<=300, last week=410, trend=up ↗
- Docs updated (team-facing): target=2, last week=1, trend=down ↘

Wins (call-out):
- Reproduced the cache eviction bug locally and wrote a failing test (big step)
- Coached Maya on canary rollback script — she shipped the runbook draft
- Cleaned up two lingering TODOs in my oncall checklist

Blockers & unresolved: (short, actionable)
- PR review backlog: reviewers busy — pinged Ryan + added a short summary comment to speed review. Action: schedule 20-min sync with Ryan Monday.
- Cache bug root cause not fully confirmed in staging. Question: do I need additional traces from prod? Who to ask for access? (Ping SRE)
- Too many ad-hoc syncs from product — need clearer triage. Action: propose weekly 15-min slot for product triage.

Habits & experiments (what I care about):
- Experiment: 2x 90-min deep blocks instead of 4x45. Goal: increase sustained focus; measure by count of context switches. Status: tried once, felt better.
- Experiment: meeting-free Wednesday morning. Outcome: helped but meetings moved to Thurs. Next: block Wed/Thu mornings for at least two sprints.

Concrete actions for next week (prioritized):
1) Finish and split infra PR: break into smaller reviewable chunks by Wed (timebox 6 hours Mon/Tue).
2) Short sync with Ryan (20m) Monday to unblock reviews.
3) Request additional staging traces + SRE pairing Tue (ENG-1142).
4) Reserve 2 x 90-min deep blocks Mon/Thu mornings and protect calendar from 10:00–13:00 on those days.
5) Draft a 15-min product triage proposal and share with PM by Wed.
6) Update oncall checklist + add quick repro steps for cache bug.

Risk assessment (if actions not taken):
- PR remains blocked -> pushes feature timeline -> increased fire drills before release window.
- Continued meeting spillover -> deep work weeks decrease -> measurable drop in PR throughput.

Quick retro notes (process learnings):
- Small, focused PRs get merged faster. Plan to break work into reviewable pieces earlier.
- Pair debugging with SRE reduced time to reproduce; schedule pair early next time.
- Explicitly communicate calendar blocks; if I don't, teammates assume availability.

Questions to self / Prompts for next entry:
- Did the 90-min blocks increase sustained focus the following week? (Yes/No + #context switches)
- Which review strategy decreased PR latency: more reviewers or smaller PRs?
- Which meetings can be consolidated or transformed into async updates?

Notes to self (short, informal):
- When blocked > 3 hours, switch to pairing mode instead of solo debugging.
- Keep PR descriptions short but include an explicit summary + testing notes (helps reviewers).
- Use the 'blocking' label in GitHub to make it visible to oncall rotation.

References / quick links (for copying into Slack):
- Linear ticket: https://linear.app/ENG/issue/ENG-1142 (cache eviction traces)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/472
- Quick runbook draft: https://confluence.internal/redwood/oncall/runbook-draft (copy in final doc)

End note: short, repeatable, obvious next actions = everything. Keep this doc as the single place I check before updating Jira/Linear.

-- Izzy

(Notes to collaborator: Maya/Ryan — feel free to add quick bullets under 'wins' or 'blockers' if you saw anything I missed. No need for formal edits; quick comments OK.)
